title: agraphis patula
intro: Agraphis patula, commonly known as the Indian pickled ginger or Indian pickering, is a plant species belonging to the Lamiaceae family. It is a perennial herb with a rich history of traditional use in Ayurvedic medicine, valued for its potential health benefits, which include reducing fever, inflammation, and digestive issues. The therapeutic actions of Agraphis patula are attributed to its bioactive constituents, such as flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which exhibit anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant properties. The plant's bioactive constituents, including rosmarinic acid and ursolic acid, are responsible for its therapeutic actions, making it a promising candidate for the development of natural remedies.
